Help Todd McCormick Celebrate his 30th Birthday in Prison October 7.
From http://www.mi4norml.org

Send Todd McCormick, who will be 30 years old next Saturday October 7th, a birthday card and tell him Michigan PRA sent you.

SeeTodd McCormick’s Letter from The Hole:
" I say that we should not fear. I'm in the heart of the monster and feel no fear. "

Todd is a medical marijuana patient and prisoner of the Clinton Administrations' continuing the bottomless money pit, the so-called " War on Drugs ". He was prosecuted with the now-dead libertarian martyr Peter McWilliams (who originally came from Michigan). This man stood up for you and is paying the price-invest a stamp in making him know you haven't forgotten him!
See
The Murder of Peter McWilliams -- An Indictment, Not an Obituary – by Richard Cowan

Todd has a severe spinal condition, tumors, cancer and the hip joint of a nine year- old child - and right this minute in solitary confinement at:

Todd Patrick McCormick
Inmate #11071-112
F.C.I.
P.O. Box 3007
Terminal Island, Ca. 90731

He is there because of draconian laws concerning a plant that helps Todd (and millions of others) deal with various diseases and conditions, pain, muscle spasms and many other medical problems.

PRA Director Gregory C. Schmid is Michigan NORML coordinator and urges all PRA people to get into NORML of Michigan www.mi4norml.org

Please contact Will at webmaster@mi4norml.org

NORML is the household name; it is a recognizable. It is our bridge to tomorrow.

In April all the NORML chapters functionally evolve into PRA chapters. Each county chapter will have phone and email for each other, but the director will also delegate a person to call people each week or so to have them turn in petitions and explain why they didn't get any. This will help determine who is dead wood, and will promote early and regular counting-checking of signatures by another person who will be responsible for doing that and for sending me regular report which can be posted on the web site. Hopefully a well established protocol will free people up to work well.

The Recruiting Director will recruit and seek petition opportunities, and coordinate those opportunities with other counties, and set regular meetings. These need to be set well in advance, and can be a a house at first or a coffee shop or anywhere you can get. Use the members to find the right spot if need be. And consider a notice in the paper-always include web site and your phone and address of the meeting is optional-you could have them call you for that.

The Petition Instructor will take people by the hand their first time out and show them the technical and practical ropes.

The Volunteer Coordinator will call the locals and send then places, check on their progress, and report to you and collect petitions for the checker.

The Checker/Reporting person will flyspeck and count petitions, report the weekly totals to me, and safeguard or send the petitions to me.We will have the QVL for you to use-this has every registered voter by county, street, or name-it will have their city-twsp and everything and will be a big help for checking petitions and also for door to door canvassing.

The Press/Promotions/ Newsletter person will coordinate op ed pieces, Press releases, and a newsletter which will not go out very often. The newsletter will basically give meeting times and places, report results, and will not be done so often as to be a burden. It will be paid for with the $5 dues and the ad sales to sponsors.

We need two meetings set up in advance at all times-these should be advertised in the paper! Get this effort underway now to avoid hurrying later to get organized.

By Kathleen Gray -August 30

Fight against legalizing marijuana gets boost

The Troy Community Coalition will receive $10,000 toward its fight to ensure marijuana won't be legalized.

The coalition recently helped sponsor a 2-day seminar to educate law enforcement and other antidrug groups about continuing efforts to legalize marijuana.

Oakland County Prosecutor David Gorcyca donated the money, which came from drug forfeitures. Supporters of a ballot proposal to legalize marijuana were unable to gather enough signatures to get the issue on the ballot. Even though it won't appear on the November ballot, the coalition plans to continue its efforts.

Opponents of efforts to legalize pot get $10,000 from county prosecutor

Other groups might be eligible for similar funding.

By:Michael Bencsik, News Reporter

August 30, 2000

The Oakland County Prosecutor's Office has donated $10,000 to a coalition that worked to defeat a ballot issue supporting the legalization of marijuana.

The money came from the prosecutor's drug forfeiture fund. The fund was established for law enforcement agencies to take the assets of people they prosecute for violating drug laws.

The money was given to the Troy Community Coalition, an organization established to fight drugs, alcohol and tobacco use. Other areas also have formed coalitions as well, such as Orion Township and Rochester Hills.

" Basically they have been monitoring these pro-drug organizations as they go around the country, " said James Halushka, chief of warrants and investigations at the prosecutor's office. " The goal was keep it (the liberalization of marijuana) off the ballot and number two, defeat it if it goes on. "

Use of the money had to be approved by the Oakland County Board of Commissioners. Commissioner and vice chairman Lawrence Obrecht voted to approve the grant, but spoke in favor of other groups also being eligible for funds.

" I wanted to make sure that other coalitions in the county would be given consideration, " he said.

Obrecht described the coalitions as " children's coalitions " that support a multitude of programs including anti-smoking and alcohol.

Obrecht said the group crosses political lines and includes everyone.

" It is kind of like going to church on Sunday - everyone goes, " he said.

Halushka said unlike forfeiture purchases for police equipment, the prosecutor has spent forfeiture money on education such as middle school anti-drug calendars.

" When we look at requests, we look at things that will benefit the county as a whole. In fact, it (the anti-legalization) benefits law enforcement statewide, " he said. " We think that this is a legitimate public health concern. "

Halushka said pro-drug legalization groups have dumped millions of dollars across the country into ballot issues. He said that led to the weakening of drug laws in places such as California and Arizona.

Prosecutor Dave Gorcyca issued a statement Tuesday saying a two-year effort to place a drug legalization referendum on the November ballot was defeated last month.

" I am certain that it was a combination of our two-year public education effort and plain old-fashioned common sense that caused Michigan voters to refuse to sign that petition, " Gorcyca said.

" My decision to use drug forfeiture funds to help defeat the drug legalization question was an easy one - ironically, it is the money of drug dealers that was used to defeat the proposal. "

Coalition fights legal pot

Conference targets medical marijuana

June 9, 1998

BY ROBERT H. CAMPBELL

Free Press Staff Writer

The Troy Community Coalition, in collaboration with several groups, has launched a pre-emptive strike against the legalization of marijuana and other drugs in Michigan.

" Watching other states deal with this issue has made us uneasy, " said Mary Ann Solberg, executive director of the coalition.

The coalition, the chief prosecutors from Oakland, Macomb and Wayne counties, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration and the Coalition of Healthy

Communities sponsored a half-day conference Monday at the Troy Marriott, " Marijuana: Myth vs. Reality. "

The event, billed as a statewide conference, was designed to raise awareness about a potential ballot initiative in Michigan, said Oakland County Prosecutor David Gorcyca.

Other states have gained the signatures needed to place the legalization of marijuana as a medication on the ballots, circumventing the state Legislature, Solberg said.

The Oakland County Health Division's office of substance abuse said there has been an increase in teenagers seeking treatment for marijuana use.

During the 1996-97 fiscal year, 51.5 percent of people younger than 20 who were admitted to treatment programs had marijuana problems, while 34.4 percent were being treated for alcohol, said John Larsen, a division program analyst.
See
The Real Data On Teen Marijuana " Abuse Treatment " – What The Media Don’t Tell Us: " Half of marijuana treatment admissions were referred through the criminal justice system. " -- Analysis By Richard Cowan

" That statistic has reversed itself in the last four or five years, " said Larsen.

Speakers at the conference included public officials from Arizona and Washington, states that have had referendums on drug legalization.

Barnett Lotstein, special assistant county prosecutor in Arizona, praised the organizers for being " way ahead of the curve. " In 1996, Arizona voters approved by 64 percent a measure that allows doctors to prescribe marijuana, heroin and LSD for medicinal purposes.

Lotstein told the crowd of about 200 that anti-legalization groups were outspent, $1.6 million to $35,000.

Washington Lt. Gov. Brad Owens said " legalizers " have been successful " because of America's complacent, 'it's-only-pot' attitude. "
See
Seattle Times Editorial Reports Washington State Lt. Governor Brad Owens Fined
For Using Tax Dollars To Campaign Against State Medical Marijuana Initiative

Allen St. Pierre, executive director of NORML, or National Organization for the Reform of Marijuana Laws, said Michigan is not an immediate target state. NORML, based in Washington, D.C., argues that marijuana laws should be changed to allow medicinal and non-medicinal use for adults.

St. Pierre said anti-reform groups should be worried because public opinion is against them. " That's why they had trouble raising money in the Arizona election.

" This same effort went on last week in Florida. It was called the Anti-Medical Marijuana Summit. It was exactly the same tone and tenor there. Plotting in advance on how to stymie voter initiatives. "

Several teens who attended Monday's event criticized it for being too political.

Marijuana is " already illegal and it doesn't make any difference. People still smoke, " said Sarah Miller, 17.

Instead you have to change people's attitudes, said Mac Vaughey, 17.
